quests.instruction: Where in the fridge is the best place for raw chicken, so its juices cannot drip onto other food?
quests.correctAnswer: The bottom shelf 🧊
options: The top shelf 🥗
Next to the butter 🧈
The bottom shelf 🧊
quests.hint: If something leaks, which way does it drip?
quests.explanation: Raw meat goes on the lowest shelf, in a covered dish, so drips cannot land on foods that are eaten without cooking.
quests.funFact: The back of a fridge is usually colder than the door.

quests.instruction: How long can cooked leftovers sit on the counter before they should go in the fridge?
quests.correctAnswer: About two hours at most ⏱️
options: Overnight, so it can cool down 🌙
A whole week, if it smells fine 📅
About two hours at most ⏱️
quests.hint: Germs grow fast in warm food.
quests.explanation: Food left out for more than about two hours can grow germs that cause tummy aches. Putting leftovers in the fridge soon keeps them safe.
quests.funFact: Hot food does not need to cool completely first. A grown-up can put it in the fridge in small containers.

quests.instruction: Someone stands in front of the open fridge deciding on a snack for a long time. What happens?
quests.correctAnswer: Cold air escapes and food warms up 🧊
options: The food gets colder, even faster ❄️
Cold air escapes and food warms up 🧊
The fridge cleans itself out 🧼
quests.hint: Consider what is trying to stay inside the fridge.
quests.explanation: An open door lets cold air out and warm air in, so food warms up and the fridge has to work harder. Decide first, then open.
quests.funFact: A fridge light turns on whenever the door opens, but the cold does not come with it.

quests.instruction: A grown-up is making vegetable soup. Which order fits the job?
quests.correctAnswer: Wash, chop, cook 🥕
options: Wash, chop, cook 🥕
Cook, chop, wash 🍲
Chop, cook, wash 🔪
quests.hint: Vegetables should be clean before anything is done to them.
quests.explanation: Vegetables are washed first, chopped next, and cooked last. Cooking before chopping does not work.
quests.funFact: Many cooks prepare everything first, so cooking goes quickly once the heat is on.

quests.instruction: Why is a kitchen sink usually near the counter and the stove?
quests.correctAnswer: Water is needed all through cooking 🚰
options: It looks tidier when it is there ✨
Water is only needed at the very end ⏰
Water is needed all through cooking 🚰
quests.hint: Work out how many times a cook rinses, fills, or washes.
quests.explanation: Cooks rinse food, fill pots, and wash hands over and over, so the sink sits close to where the work happens.
quests.funFact: Many kitchens are planned around a triangle of fridge, sink, and stove so that walking between them is short.

quests.instruction: A grown-up is chopping on the counter. Where is the safest helpful spot for a child to stand?
quests.correctAnswer: At the side, away from the stove 🧑
options: At the side, away from the stove 🧑
Right next to the burner 🔥
Behind the person holding the knife 🔪
quests.hint: Stay away from both the heat and the sharp tool.
quests.explanation: Standing to one side, away from the stove, keeps you clear of heat, and in view of the grown-up. Right behind someone with a knife is a bump waiting to happen.
quests.funFact: Cooks call out 'behind you!' in busy restaurant kitchens, so nobody collides.

quests.instruction: Which cup is best for a small child's juice?
quests.correctAnswer: A plastic cup 🥤
options: A thin glass 🥛
A plastic cup 🥤
A china teacup 🍵
quests.hint: Pick the one that will not break if it is dropped.
quests.explanation: A plastic cup is light and does not shatter, so it is safer for small hands. Glass and china can break into sharp pieces.
quests.funFact: Many children's cups have wide bases so they are harder to knock over.

quests.instruction: A warm drink in a cup with a handle: why is the handle useful?
quests.correctAnswer: You can hold it without touching the hot side ☕
options: It makes the drink taste a lot sweeter 🍬
You can hold it without touching the hot side ☕
It stops the cup from rolling off the table 🎯
quests.hint: Think about which part of the cup gets warm.
quests.explanation: A handle keeps your fingers away from the hot side of the cup. Hot drinks are for grown-ups, and a child should ask for help.
quests.funFact: Mugs with handles have been made for hundreds of years.

quests.instruction: A spoon falls on the kitchen floor in the middle of dinner. What should happen to it?
quests.correctAnswer: It gets washed before it is used again 🧼
options: It gets washed before it is used again 🧼
It goes straight back onto the table 🥄
It gets a quick wipe on someone's sleeve 👕
quests.hint: The floor has things on it that food should not touch.
quests.explanation: The floor carries dirt and germs, so a dropped spoon is washed before anyone eats with it. A wipe on a sleeve does not clean it.
quests.funFact: A clean spoon from the drawer takes a few seconds to fetch.

quests.instruction: Cookies come out of the oven. Which part of the oven is still very hot?
quests.correctAnswer: The door and the inside 🔥
options: Only the little light 💡
The door and the inside 🔥
Nothing, it cools instantly ❄️
quests.hint: Metal and glass stay hot for a long time after heating.
quests.explanation: An oven stays hot for a while after it is turned off, and its door gets hot too. Stay back and let a grown-up deal with it.
quests.funFact: Oven gloves are thick so that heat takes much longer to reach a hand.

quests.instruction: The cookie tray is done. Who should take it out of a hot oven?
quests.correctAnswer: A grown-up with oven gloves 🧤
options: Anyone holding a thin kitchen towel 🧻
A grown-up with oven gloves 🧤
A child who is tall enough to reach 🧒
quests.hint: Taking something out of an oven needs protection and strong arms.
quests.explanation: Hot trays can burn through a thin towel, and a child could drop the tray. Oven gloves and an adult are the safe pair.
quests.funFact: Heat can pass through a damp cloth faster than through a dry one.

quests.instruction: A pot is heating on the stove and the grown-up goes to answer the door. What should you do?
quests.correctAnswer: Stay clear and call them back 📣
options: Stay clear and call them back 📣
Turn up the heat to help 🔥
Taste the food with your finger ☝️
quests.hint: A pot on a stove is not something to look after alone.
quests.explanation: Hot food and a hot stove are for adults to manage, so call the grown-up back. Turning the heat up or touching the food could burn you.
quests.funFact: Many stoves have knobs that are hard for small hands to turn on purpose.

quests.instruction: A child wants to help make fruit salad. Which tool is safest for them to use?
quests.correctAnswer: A child-safe knife with a grown-up 🧑‍🍳
options: A child-safe knife with a grown-up 🧑‍🍳
A big chef's knife for chopping 🔪
A sharp grater used all alone 🧀
quests.hint: Look for a tool made for small hands and an adult close by.
quests.explanation: A child-safe knife is blunt and made for small hands, and the grown-up stays near. A chef's knife or a grater can cut skin badly.
quests.funFact: Soft fruit like banana can be cut with a plastic knife.

quests.instruction: Where are knives best stored in a home with children?
quests.correctAnswer: In a block or drawer out of reach 🔪
options: Loose in a sink full of soapy water 🚰
In a block or drawer out of reach 🔪
Resting on the edge of the counter 🍽️
quests.hint: A hidden sharp edge or an easy-to-grab one are the problems.
quests.explanation: Knives stay in a block or a drawer, away from small hands. In a sink full of water they cannot be seen, and on the counter edge they can fall.
quests.funFact: Knife blocks keep each blade covered so that nobody reaches in by accident.

quests.instruction: A knife slides off the counter and falls. What should you do?
quests.correctAnswer: Step back and tell a grown-up 🙋
options: Try to catch it with your hands ✋
Grab it quickly by the blade 🔪
Step back and tell a grown-up 🙋
quests.hint: A falling knife is not something to stop with your hands.
quests.explanation: Stepping back keeps your feet and hands away from the blade. A grown-up can pick it up safely.
quests.funFact: Cooks never try to catch a falling knife, and they let it drop.

quests.instruction: Which spill is the most dangerous to step in?
quests.correctAnswer: Cooking oil on a hard floor 🫒
options: A few dry crumbs from toast 🍞
A dried leaf from the garden 🍃
Cooking oil on a hard floor 🫒
quests.hint: Look for the one that makes the floor slide under your feet.
quests.explanation: Oil makes a smooth floor extremely slippery. Crumbs and leaves are easy to see and can be swept up.
quests.funFact: Oil and water do not mix, so wiping with only water can spread the oil.

quests.instruction: Juice spills across the kitchen table. What is the best first step?
quests.correctAnswer: Wipe it up with a cloth 🧽
options: Wipe it up with a cloth 🧽
Wait for it to dry by itself ⏳
Pour a cup of water on it 💧
quests.hint: A sticky puddle gets worse the longer it sits.
quests.explanation: Wiping a spill right away stops it from dripping on the floor or getting sticky. Waiting or adding water makes it spread.
quests.funFact: Sugar in juice dries into a sticky film that takes extra scrubbing.

quests.instruction: Why is a spill on a tile floor more slippery than on a carpet?
quests.correctAnswer: The tile does not soak it up 🏠
options: The tile is a little warmer 🔥
The carpet is always a bit damp 💧
The tile does not soak it up 🏠
quests.hint: Think about what carpet does with liquids.
quests.explanation: A carpet takes up the liquid into its fibers, but tile leaves it as a puddle on top. That slippery layer is what causes falls.
quests.funFact: Mats near sinks soak up drips so floors stay safer.

quests.instruction: A bottle of dish soap looks a lot like a juice bottle. How can you tell the difference?
quests.correctAnswer: Read the label and ask a grown-up 📝
options: Smell it to find out 👃
Taste a tiny drop to check 👅
Read the label and ask a grown-up 📝
quests.hint: Colors and shapes can be misleading, but words are not.
quests.explanation: Labels tell you what is inside. If you cannot read it or are not sure, a grown-up can check. Smelling or tasting unknown liquids can be harmful.
quests.funFact: Cleaning products often have bright colors that can look like drinks, which is why they are stored up high.

quests.instruction: Cleaning products should stay in their original bottles. Why?
quests.correctAnswer: The label tells everyone what is inside 🏷️
options: The label tells everyone what is inside 🏷️
They stay colder and fresher 🧊
They smell nicer in the cupboard 🌸
quests.hint: Think about what is printed on the bottle.
quests.explanation: The original label shows what is inside and how to use it safely. A cleaner poured into a drink bottle could be mistaken for something to drink.
quests.funFact: Labels often list first-aid steps, in case a product is swallowed or splashed.

quests.instruction: What does a warning symbol on a cleaning bottle tell you?
quests.correctAnswer: Take care: it can be harmful ⚠️
options: It means it is safe to drink 🥤
Take care: it can be harmful ⚠️
It is a picture on a toy 🧸
quests.hint: The word warning is in the name.
quests.explanation: A warning symbol means the product can hurt eyes, skin, or lungs if used wrongly. Adults read the label before using it.
quests.funFact: Different shapes and colors mean different dangers, such as flames or corrosion.

quests.instruction: Why do we wash greasy plates with warm water and soap, not just cold water?
quests.correctAnswer: Soap and warm water lift the grease 🧼
options: Cold water melts the plates away 🧊
Warm water makes dishes much lighter ⚖️
Soap and warm water lift the grease 🧼
quests.hint: Grease sticks to a plate like oil to water.
quests.explanation: Grease does not dissolve in cold water. Warm water and soap break it up so it can be rinsed away.
quests.funFact: Dish soap works because it holds on to both grease and water.

quests.instruction: Which sponge habit keeps dishes clean?
quests.correctAnswer: Rinsing and wringing out the sponge 🧽
options: Leaving it in a bowl of dirty water 💧
Rinsing and wringing out the sponge 🧽
Using it to wipe the floor too 🧹
quests.hint: A sponge that stays wet and grubby grows germs.
quests.explanation: A rinsed, squeezed sponge dries and stays fresher. A soaking sponge or one that wiped the floor would spread germs onto your dishes.
quests.funFact: Sponges are best replaced often because they hold moisture and food bits.

quests.instruction: The kitchen is clean and the wiping cloth is damp. What is the best place for it?
quests.correctAnswer: Hung up to dry 🧽
options: Hung up to dry 🧽
Left in the sink 🚰
Folded into the cupboard 🗄️
quests.hint: A damp cloth needs air before it can be used again.
quests.explanation: A hung cloth dries quickly and stays fresh. A damp cloth folded away or left in the sink grows germs and smells.
quests.funFact: Some kitchens have a rail under the sink or beside the oven for drying cloths.

quests.instruction: Why do we rinse fruit and vegetables before eating them?
quests.correctAnswer: To wash off dirt and germs 🍎
options: To make them taste sweeter 🍯
To wash off dirt and germs 🍎
To make them a little heavier ⚖️
quests.hint: Ask yourself where they were growing and who touched them.
quests.explanation: Fruit and vegetables can carry dirt and germs from the soil, the market, or hands. A good rinse helps get them off.
quests.funFact: Washing under running water works better than soaking.

quests.instruction: Which two foods should be kept apart while a grown-up prepares a meal?
quests.correctAnswer: Raw meat and salad 🥩
options: Raw meat and salad 🥩
Bread and butter slices 🍞
Rice and cooked beans 🍚
quests.hint: One of them will be cooked, and one will not.
quests.explanation: Raw meat can carry germs that cooking kills, but salad is eaten raw. Keeping them apart, with separate boards, stops germs from spreading.
quests.funFact: Many kitchens use a different chopping board for raw meat.

quests.instruction: A yogurt pot's date says it ran out last week. What should you do?
quests.correctAnswer: Show it to a grown-up first 📅
options: Eat it up quickly 🥣
Show it to a grown-up first 📅
Smell it and then decide 👃
quests.hint: Dates are there to help, and grown-ups know how to read them.
quests.explanation: A date that has passed means the food may not be safe. A grown-up can check it and decide, since smell alone does not show everything.
quests.funFact: Some labels say 'use by', which is about safety, and some say 'best before', which is about quality.

quests.instruction: Steam is rising from a boiling pot. What is the safest place for a child to stand?
quests.correctAnswer: Well back from the stove 🚶
options: With a face right over the pot 👀
Touching the pot handle 🖐️
Well back from the stove 🚶
quests.hint: Steam can burn skin even without touching the pot.
quests.explanation: Steam and hot pots burn quickly. Standing back keeps you safe, and a grown-up can answer your questions from there.
quests.funFact: Steam from boiling water is hotter than the water itself.

quests.instruction: You are very hungry while dinner is cooking. Which is the best choice?
quests.correctAnswer: Ask for a safe snack like fruit 🍎
options: Taste straight from the hot pot 🍲
Reach into the hot oven 🔥
Ask for a safe snack like fruit 🍎
quests.hint: Choose something that does not need a stove.
quests.explanation: Asking for a ready-to-eat snack keeps you away from heat and gives dinner time to finish.
quests.funFact: A piece of fruit or some bread is a quick, safe snack.

quests.instruction: Which of these should you tell a grown-up about right away?
quests.correctAnswer: A pan handle over the edge 🍳
options: A pan handle over the edge 🍳
A bowl of fruit on the table 🍎
A clean dish towel hanging on a hook 🧺
quests.hint: Which one could be knocked off the stove in a second?
quests.explanation: A pan handle sticking out can be bumped, and a hot pan could spill. A grown-up can turn it inward.
quests.funFact: Cooks turn pan handles inward as a habit.
